records.name: Ağrı
records.current_summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): far east; conservative. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025) reports a leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus '11th Judicial Package' that would open the way to criminal charges against LGBT people — called one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades: conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' including its so-called 'promotion' would bring up to three years in prison, participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies up to four years (same-sex marriage is not legal, so such ceremonies are by definition symbolic), and gender-affirming care would be restricted (surgery age raised from 18 to 25, mandatory permanent infertility), with medical professionals fined or imprisoned up to seven years and transgender patients up to three years for care outside the new limits, forcing treatment into underground settings. It contains no Ağrı-specific provision; the source supports this record's claim that this national framework is what a visitor stands under in the province.

Kaos GL's report on 2025 ('A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy') documents six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected (counted from media and civil-society reports because the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics), 89 torture or ill-treatment violations (up from 51), mostly linked to peaceful assembly, and 336 assembly and 313 liberty violations — a roughly 2.5-fold liberty increase mostly of detentions — with event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings. It reports hostility institutionalised under 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events, presented as national practice rather than provincial choice. No Ağrı-specific finding appears; the source supports this record's claims about the country-wide framework.

records.name: Amasya
records.current_summary:
This province has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; what a trans visitor here stands under is the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked draft omnibus justice package from October 2025 (the '11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people across Turkiye - Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades - and it contains no province-specific provisions. The LGBTI+ association Kaos GL reported that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as state policy under a 'Year of the Family' banner, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions creating a climate encouraging rights violations.

Because the surviving record is entirely national-level and carries no provincial breakdown, neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 Oct 2025) on the leaked '11th Judicial Package' draft omnibus law: would amend the Turkish penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', criminalise taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (penalties up to 4 years in prison), raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility, and punish health professionals who perform such care - HRW calls it one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades, and 15 Turkish LGBT groups plus the Turkish Medical Association oppose the draft.

Kaos GL report launch on the 2025 report 'A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy': documents that anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as explicit state policy, with senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate that encouraged human-rights violations, and regulatory/supervisory bodies systematically restricting freedom of expression and artistic freedom; findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the launch.

records.name: Bitlis
records.current_summary:
Every province in Türkiye sits under the same intensifying national framework. A leaked draft of the 11th Judicial Package (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and 4 years for same-sex ceremonies — and would raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report ('A Major Siege', published February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — presidency-centred, implemented through the family ministry — documenting 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5-fold), counted from media coverage because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics.

No province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors in Bitlis was documented in this research pass; the national framework above is the whole documented picture for Bitlis. The absence of recorded provincial enforcement is not evidence of local tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban.
